concepts.title: Whole Genome Targeted and Metagenomics Sequencing

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Whole Genome Targeted and Metagenomics Sequencing' refers to.
questions.a: Sequencing projects come in flavours: whole genome sequencing - reference-guided or de novo - reads everything from Haemophilus influenzae onward including the 1990-2003 human effort; targeted and clinical exome sequencing PCR-amplify only disease-linked regions; RNASeq counts transcripts, ChipSeq maps regulator binding; and metagenomics sequences whole microbial communities straight from gut, spring or soil without culturing, hunting novel heat-stable enzymes.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Whole Genome Targeted and Metagenomics Sequencing'.
questions.a: Match the project to the question - everything, a panel, the transcriptome, binding sites or a whole community.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Whole Genome Targeted and Metagenomics Sequencing' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Genome Editing with Transposons and CRISPR-Cas9

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Genome Editing with Transposons and CRISPR-Cas9' refers to.
questions.a: Genome engineering rewrites DNA on purpose: engineered transposons - the cut-and-paste jumping genes - knock out genes by insertional disruption or knock in new sequences, while the CRISPR-Cas9 system pairs a guide RNA with Cas9 endonuclease to cut a chosen site, letting non-homologous end joining knock the gene out or homologous recombination with a supplied template knock in the corrected version - the bacterial immune memory repurposed by Charpentier and Doudna's 2020 Nobel work.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Genome Editing with Transposons and CRISPR-Cas9'.
questions.a: Position the cut with a guide RNA, then let the cell's repair choice decide knockout or precise knock-in.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Genome Editing with Transposons and CRISPR-Cas9' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Structural Functional and Comparative Genomics' refers to.
questions.a: Computational genomics turns sequence floods into biology on GPU-accelerated clusters, with three lenses: structural genomics solves or organises the 3D folds of every encoded protein and the physical layout of chromosomes; functional genomics asks what the genome does through RNASeq, ChipSeq and metagenomics; comparative genomics aligns species to find core and unique genes, annotate new genomes and root phylogenies - supported by India's three national genomics core facilities.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Structural Functional and Comparative Genomics'.
questions.a: One genome, three questions - what shape, what job, and what is shared or unique among relatives.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Structural Functional and Comparative Genomics' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Protein Engineering from Tags to Immunotoxins

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Protein Engineering from Tags to Immunotoxins' refers to.
questions.a: Rational protein engineering rewrites codons for new tricks: a Met-to-Ala point mutation at position 222 makes the detergent enzyme subtilisin bleach-proof while its Ser221-His64-Asp32 triad keeps cutting; a fused six-histidine tag grabs nickel columns for one-step purification; a GFP fusion glows to reveal where a protein lives; single-chain variable fragments fused to Pseudomonas or diphtheria toxins build immunotoxins that hunt cancer cells; and mouse antibodies are humanised for therapy.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Protein Engineering from Tags to Immunotoxins'.
questions.a: Change the codon, change the property - stability, purification handles, location tags or targeted cell killers.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Protein Engineering from Tags to Immunotoxins' taught, and from which source text?
